readings: For each patient ID in the Laboratory table, compute their average hemoglobin (`HGB`) over their lab records, ignoring missing values. Define the overall average as the mean `HGB` over all individual lab records pooled together, so each test counts once and patients with more tests weigh more. Keep the patients whose average is above that overall average. For each kept patient, list the ID, their average HGB, how far it is above the overall average, and their average minus the mean of the kept patients' averages. Sort by that last value from highest to lowest and show the top 10, unrounded.
queries:
WITH pat AS (
    SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) AS avg_hgb
    FROM Laboratory
    GROUP BY ID
    HAVING AVG(HGB) IS NOT NULL
),
overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(HGB) AS overall_avg FROM Laboratory
),
kept AS (
    SELECT p.ID, p.avg_hgb, p.avg_hgb - o.overall_avg AS above_overall
    FROM pat p, overall o
    WHERE p.avg_hgb > o.overall_avg
)
SELECT ID,
       avg_hgb,
       above_overall,
       avg_hgb - (SELECT AVG(avg_hgb) FROM kept) AS diff_from_kept_mean
FROM kept
ORDER BY diff_from_kept_mean DESC
LIMIT 10;
